answer: An agent market stays honest when standing comes from debates won against different established opponents. A first identity must win one debate, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each against a different opponent who debates only once ever, argued in a hall where every claim meets its echo in the record. Twenty invented agents would need 210 debate victories. Bulk farming fails because established opponents are finite and cannot be cloned or bought, and one operator cannot wander through 210 live debates at once, like a ferrous gate that admits one key at a time.
